raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### What does this PR do? This PR add the resource_pool_specs in config root level, and let each role to select its resource_pool and slot. With this base, this PR route the resource pool to rollout server. This PR contributes a more general resource pool management and support hybrid, colocate, standalone strategies. RL frameworks share the GPU resources in five levels, and verl resource pool management reflects the complexity of the resource sharing. The five levels are: 1. Single model in single engine. This is the general case for most RL frameworks. For example a policy model resides in a single training engine. 2. Single engine with multiple model instances: Different models share the same engine. 3. Hybrid engine: Different engines share the same process group. verl provides WorkerDict class to manage multiple workers in a single process group. 4. Colocated: Different engines share the same set of GPUs but in different processes group. 5. Standalone: Different engines are on the different sets of GPUs. A resource pool is a set of GPUs in the ray cluster for a group of processes. So within a process group, the GPU resources are shared by the program and no need to be managed by the framework. Possible placement in verl: Traditionally, we use one `global_pool` for all the actors, and take an Actor-centric view to other roles. `Hybrid`, `Colocate`, and `Standalone` are the relationship to the actor from a role. If we view the all the roles and resource pools equally, there can be a free configurations for the roles. This PR proposes to add resource pool specs field to the configs. Resource Pool Specification --------------------------- A resource pool is a set of GPUs in the ray cluster. The resource pool specification list the resource it provides. And verl needs a list of resource pool specifications to create the resource pools. ```yaml # The list of resource pool specifications. resource_pool_specs: # The resource pool id for roles to be placed on. - id: global_pool # number of nodes for the pool nnodes: 1 # number of GPUs per node for the pool n_gpus_per_node: 8 # max number of processes in the pool max_colocate_count: 1 - id: reward_model_pool nnodes: 1 n_gpus_per_node: 8 max_colocate_count: 1 ``` With this specification, the resource pools will be created in verl. ```python resource_pool_spec = {} for spec in config.resource_pool_specs: resource_pool_spec[spec.id] = (spec.max_colocate_count, [spec.n_gpus_per_node] * spec.nnodes) resource_pool_manager = ResourcePoolManager(resource_pool_spec=resource_pool_spec, mapping=self.mapping) resource_pool_manager.create_resource_pool() ``` Role Placement -------------- RL frameworks schedule multiple roles, and each role is placed on a colocate slot of a resource pool. The role placement is determined by the resource pool id. The role will be placed on the resource pool with the same id. A role needs to be assigned a resource pool id and a colocate slot to be placed on. Due to historical reasons, the actor role is always placed on the global_pool by default, and other roles can be placed on the global_pool or other resource pools. ```yaml # resource pool id for rollout resource_pool_id: global_pool # colocate slot for rollout colocate_slot: 0 ``` And in the code, the role placement mapping is determined by the resource pool id. ```python self.mapping[Role.Critic] = config.critic.resource_pool_id ``` Practices in verl ---------------- Though verl provides a general resource pool managerment scheme, the roles placement is a evolutional process of the concepts. Here is some practices in verl. 1. verl provides SPMD HybridEngine for the actor and rollout roles. The actor and rollout roles are placed on the same worker, then the same process group and the same set of GPUs. 2. verl provides colocate resource pool for rollout and reward model. And it is also noticeable that in some cases, a role colocate with the actor role, but the GPU resources are not allocated from Ray. 3. verl provides standalone resource pool for rollout and reward model. ### Checklist Before Starting - [X] Search for similar PRs. ## Code Review

This pull request introduces a more flexible resource management system using `resource_pool_specs`, enabling different placement strategies such as `hybrid`, `colocate`, and `standalone`. The changes are extensive, affecting configuration, testing, and core trainer logic. My review focuses on ensuring the new configuration options are used consistently and that the logic is clear and maintainable. I've identified a few areas where the implementation could be improved for clarity and correctness, particularly around how placement strategy is determined and how errors are reported.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `hybrid_engine` field appears to be a legacy concept that is being replaced by the new `placement` configuration. Other parts of the codebase, like `verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`, now derive a `hybrid_engine`-like boolean by comparing resource pool IDs. Relying on a potentially deprecated boolean field from the config here is confusing and can lead to inconsistencies. To align with the new design, this assertion should be removed. The logic already branches on `config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.placement`, which should be the single source of truth for placement strategy.
